question: What global growth rate for 2026 will the IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook project?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is the July 2026 Update's 3.0%. Over 2016-2025, the July-to-October current-year revision was 0 in 4 of 9 cases and otherwise ±0.1-0.2, so the base case is to hold at 3.0. IMF signals since July ('firmed at around 3 percent' in September; 'on track for around 3 percent' from Kozack on Oct 1) point to a hold, with AI capex and US resilience giving modest upside (as in Oct 2025's +0.2) and new US Iran sanctions/oil/stalled disinflation giving downside. Polymarket's 2026 world-GDP-growth markets are about realized growth with Jan 2027 close, a near-miss contract and not an anchor: 3.0 at 0.35, 3.1 at 0.28, <=2.9 at 0.22, 3.2 at 0.06. Rough discrete view: 3.0 ~50%, 3.1 ~25%, 2.9 ~14%, 3.2 ~6%, other ~5%.
calls.dossier:
- IMF WEO path for 2026 global growth: Jan 2026 Update 3.3; Apr 2026 WEO 3.1; Jul 8 2026 Update 3.0 (2027: 3.4), 'broadly unchanged cumulatively from April'. Narrative: the war shock weighs on energy importers, AI-driven demand lifts tech-value-chain economies. July raised 2026 global headline inflation to 4.7% on a projected ~32% oil price rise (IMF Jul 2026 Update; Wall Street Times summary).
- Early Sep 2026 (G20 meeting, Asheville): Georgieva said 'Since April, the global growth outlook for 2026 has firmed at around 3 percent.' She said the energy shock was weathered via reserves, new sources and demand management, and that AI investment is driving the US and Korea. She flagged debt near 100% of GDP, energy risks, stalled disinflation and imbalances (Profit/Pakistan Today, 2026-09-04).
- ~Oct 1 2026 Kozack briefing (Reuters via Arab News): 'We remain on track for world growth of around 3 percent but uncertainty...continues to remain high.' A fuller assessment comes at the Annual Meetings, including the impact of new US sanctions on Iran.
- Oct 2026 WEO: analytical chapters Oct 5-6; full report Oct 13 at the Bangkok Annual Meetings (IMF WEO page). Some search-engine summaries quote '3.0 percent for 2026 and 3.4 for 2027' as if it were the October figure; that text matches the July Update and is not confirmed October content.
- Historical July-Update-to-October-WEO revisions to current-year global growth: 2016 0 (3.1->3.1), 2017 +0.1 (3.5->3.6), 2018 -0.2 (3.9->3.7), 2019 -0.2 (3.2->3.0), 2021 -0.1 (6.0->5.9), 2022 0 (3.2->3.2), 2023 0 (3.0->3.0), 2024 0 (3.2->3.2), 2025 +0.2 (3.0->3.2). Unchanged in 4/9; SD ~0.125pp (from memory of past WEOs, not re-verified this run).
- Upside factors: AI capex and US resilience; 'firmed' language in September; 2025 precedent of an October upgrade after mid-year resilience.
- Downside factors: new US sanctions on Iran (oil supply risk), elevated and volatile commodity prices, stalled disinflation, high debt.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the Chapter 1 / executive-summary headline 2026 global growth figure in the October 2026 WEO, not the 2027 figure and not later outturns. Annulled if the full report isn't out by Oct 16.
- Event window: report release ~Oct 13 2026; as of Oct 5 2026 the figure is unpublished.
- Searched, absent: any leak or preview of the October 2026 number, the text of Georgieva's 2026 curtain-raiser speech (results surfaced older years), and a direct-match prediction market (Polymarket contracts are on realized 2026 world GDP growth, closing Jan 2027).

calls.reasoning: Over 2017-2025, the IMF's current-year global growth figure was unchanged between the July Update and the October WEO in about half the years, and moved by 0.1-0.2 points otherwise. July 2026 put it at 3.0%. In September Georgieva said the outlook 'firmed at around 3 percent', Kozack said 'on track for around 3 percent', and the OECD raised its 2026 figure by 0.1 to 2.9%; AI investment is also supporting growth. Pointing down: the war escalated, Hormuz traffic is reportedly at about a quarter of normal, and disinflation has stalled. Modal outcome is 3.0 (~45%), then 3.1 (~30%), 2.9 (~15%), 3.2 (~7%). Polymarket's realized-2026-growth markets (thin volume; resolve on realized growth, not this projection) price <=2.9 at 0.22, 3.0 at 0.35, 3.1 at 0.28 and 3.2 at 0.06: broadly consistent, used as evidence only.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual core: the July figure is 3.0, IMF messaging says 'around 3%', the OECD raised its figure to 2.9, oil is elevated and the war has escalated. Disputed facts: (1) whether Kozack explicitly restated 3.0/3.4 on Oct 1, where Run 3 relied on a search summary and Run 2 had only a snippet; this can't be settled offline, but either way the message is a hold. (2) Hormuz flows: a UAO report of ~25% of normal versus Kpler crude flows above pre-war; also unsettled, but Brent spot is $101-114, above the July path. The rest is judgment about whether upside or downside is stronger. I take a roughly balanced view with a slightly fatter tail on 3.1, keeping the mode at 3.0 and carrying forward the shared reference class.
